title: A US visa rejection couldn't stop him. NASA came looking for him instead.

sources.text: The Tribune, 2026 - From a Tractor Driver's Hut to the Halls of NASA: The Extraordinary Rise of India's Rocket Scientist
Indian Startup News, 2024 - Meet the truck driver's son who launched India's first reusable hybrid rocket, RHUMI-1

caption:
A US visa rejection couldn't stop him. NASA came looking for him instead.

Born to a tractor driver's family in rural India, he walked nearly six kilometres daily to school, dropped out of college once, then rebuilt his path by shifting from computer science to aeronautical engineering. Years earlier, his US visa application for advanced aerospace research had been rejected.

On August 24, 2024, Space Zone India - founded with his own father as first partner - launched RHUMI-1, India's first reusable hybrid rocket, from a mobile launch pad. The achievement positioned Space Zone India among Asia's emerging private space innovators. In 2026, he was selected among only 23 experts worldwide for a US State Department leadership programme with advanced NASA technical exposure.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 doesn't need permission from anyone else's institution to prove its capability - it needs people who build first, credential later. The visa that was once denied became irrelevant the moment the rocket flew.
